source.title: Business Profits Tax (BPT)
The Bureau of Revenue & Taxation: taxes (PGST, BPT, GRT, wages and salary tax, non-resident withholding, excise and other taxes)

rows.label: Business profits tax (BPT)
rows.note: net income (gross revenue less allowable deductions) of every PGST-registered person, for each tax year. Business Profits Tax (BPT) applies to all PGST-registered businesses, including foreign-investment certificate holders, the listed state-owned enterprises and banks; it replaced the gross revenue tax for them from 1 January 2023. A company's tax year ends on its balance date; for other taxpayers it is the calendar year.

source.title: Business Profits Tax (BPT)

rows.label: Business profits tax: instalments, return and losses
rows.value: Quarterly instalments of 25% of the previous year's BPT (2% of quarterly gross revenue when there was no BPT payable), due by the 15th day of the month after each quarter of the tax year; annual return within 3 months of the year end; losses carried forward 4 years
rows.note: The Bureau's page gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: Business Profits Tax (BPT)

rows.label: Gross revenue tax (GRT): businesses not registered for PGST
rows.note: quarterly gross revenue of businesses not registered for PGST (no deductions except the wage deductions). Businesses below the PGST registration threshold that have not registered for PGST remain on the gross revenue tax; they may register voluntarily. The Bureau's page gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

rows.value: Deductions: 100% of wages paid to Palauan citizen employees; up to $5,000 a quarter of wages paid to non-citizen employees; 200% of wages paid to employees holding a skilled labor certificate
rows.note: The Bureau's page gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).
